Toast notifications are a crucial element in modern web applications and websites, providing users with timely and relevant information.
When designed and implemented correctly, toast notifications can significantly enhance user engagement and interaction. In this article, we will explore the best practices for crafting engaging notification content, timing and placement strategies, and accessibility considerations to ensure that your toast notifications are effective and user-friendly.

## Crafting Engaging Notification Content

The content of your toast notifications plays a vital role in capturing users' attention and conveying the intended message. To craft engaging notification content, consider the following best practices:

### Writing Clear and Concise Messages

When writing toast notification messages, clarity and concision are paramount. Users should be able to quickly understand the purpose of the notification without having to read through lengthy text. Here are some tips for writing clear and concise messages:

* Keep messages short and to the point

...

* Use user data and preferences to inform notification content
* Allow users to customize notification settings and preferences
* Use user behavior and activity to trigger notifications
* Provide users with relevant and timely information based on their interests and needs

The following diagram illustrates the process of crafting engaging notification content:

```
graph LR;
    A["User Action"] --> B["Trigger Notification"];
    B --> C{"Relevant Information?"};
    C -->|"Yes"| D["Personalize Notification"];
    C -->|"No"| E["Dismiss Notification"];
    D --> F["Display Notification"];
```

## Timing and Placement Strategies

The timing and placement of toast notifications can significantly impact their effectiveness. To maximize user engagement, consider the following best practices for timing and placement:

### Determining the Optimal Display Duration
The display duration of toast notifications should be long enough for users to read and understand the message, but not so long that it becomes intrusive or annoying. Here are some guidelines for determining the optimal display duration:

* Display notifications for a minimum of 5-7 seconds to allow users to read the message
* Adjust display duration based on the length and complexity of the notification message
* Consider user preferences and behavior when determining display duration
* Ensure that notifications are not displayed for too long, as this can lead to user frustration

### Choosing the Right Placement on the Screen

The placement of toast notifications on the screen can also impact their effectiveness. Here are some best practices for choosing the right placement:

* Display notifications in a consistent location on the screen to establish user expectations
* Avoid displaying notifications in areas that may be distracting or intrusive, such as the center of the screen
* Consider user behavior and preferences when determining notification placement
* Ensure that notifications do not overlap with other important content or UI elements

### Avoiding Notification Overload

Notification overload can lead to user frustration and decreased engagement. To avoid notification overload, consider the following strategies:

* Limit the number of notifications displayed to users within a certain time period
* Prioritize notifications based on relevance and importance
* Allow users to customize notification settings and preferences
* Provide users with options to dismiss or snooze notifications

The following table summarizes the best practices for timing and placement:

|Best Practice |Description |
| --- | --- |
|Optimal Display Duration |Display notifications for 5-7 seconds |
|Consistent Placement |Display notifications in a consistent location on the screen |
|Avoid Notification Overload |Limit the number of notifications displayed to users |
## Accessibility Considerations

Toast notifications should be designed and implemented with accessibility in mind to ensure that they are usable by all users, including those with disabilities. Here are some best practices for accessibility considerations:

### Designing for Users with Disabilities

When designing toast notifications, consider the needs of users with disabilities, including visual, auditory, and cognitive disabilities. Here are some strategies for designing accessible notifications:

* Use clear and simple language in notification messages
* Provide alternative formats for notifications, such as text or audio
* Ensure that notifications are compatible with assistive technologies, such as screen readers
* Consider user preferences and needs when designing notifications

### Ensuring Notifications are Screen Reader Friendly
Screen readers are essential for users with visual disabilities, and toast notifications should be designed to be compatible with these technologies. Here are some best practices for ensuring screen reader compatibility:

* Use ARIA attributes to provide screen readers with notification content
* Ensure that notifications are announced by screen readers in a timely and accurate manner
* Test notifications with screen readers to ensure compatibility
* Provide alternative formats for notifications, such as text or audio

### Providing Alternatives for Users Who Prefer Not to Receive Notifications

Some users may prefer not to receive toast notifications, and it is essential to provide alternatives for these users. Here are some strategies for providing alternatives:

* Allow users to customize notification settings and preferences
* Provide alternative formats for notifications, such as email or SMS

...

By following the best practices outlined in this article, you can create notifications that enhance user engagement and interaction with your web application or website.

1. [W3C Web Accessibility Initiative](https://www.w3.org/WAI/)
2. [Material Design - Notifications](https://material.io/components/snackbars)
3. [Apple Human Interface Guidelines - Notifications](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/macos/user-interaction/notifications)
4. [Toast Notifications: A Study on User Experience](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/B9780128123456000123)

## FAQ

### Q: What is the optimal display duration for toast notifications?

A: The optimal display duration for toast notifications is between 5-7 seconds, depending on the length and complexity of the notification message.

### Q: How can I avoid notification overload?
A: To avoid notification overload, limit the number of notifications displayed to users within a certain time period, prioritize notifications based on relevance and importance, and allow users to customize notification settings and preferences.

### Q: How can I make toast notifications accessible to users with disabilities?

A: To make toast notifications accessible to users with disabilities, use clear and simple language, provide alternative formats for notifications, ensure compatibility with assistive technologies, and consider user preferences and needs when designing notifications.

# What is a toast notification? Best practices for UX

[](https://blog.logrocket.com/author/iwalolasobowale/)

[Iwalola Sobowale](https://blog.logrocket.com/author/iwalolasobowale/) A mum of two vivacious boys leading Product and User Research and championing digital innovation through my newsletter and podcast, [The Spotlight](https://podcasters.spotify.com/pod/show/iwalola-sobowale) . Catch up with my podcast and follow me on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/iwalolasobowale/ ) . Let's chat!

If figuring out when to use toast notifications feels as tricky as making the perfect toast, you’re not alone!

Bell Notification on Mobile Screen

Choosing the right notification type to implement in your design can be challenging because it’s a crucial element in ensuring a smooth user experience. But don’t worry — this article will guide you through the ins and outs of toast notifications.
You’ll learn the appropriate scenarios to use them, best practices, common pitfalls, and hear practical examples from familiar products.

Let’s get started!

_**Editor’s note:** This blog was rewritten 9 June 2025 by [Daniel Schwarz](https://blog.logrocket.com/author/danielschwarz/) to expand on the original by covering best practices, appropriate use cases, and accessibility considerations. It also updates the discussion by explaining the distinctions between similar notification types and emphasizes practical design tips to enhance user experience._

## What is a toast notification?

In simple terms, toast notifications are auto-dismissing status messages used to convey information without disrupting user workflows. They’re called “toast” notifications because they “pop up” on the screen like toast! But unlike popups/dialogs, toast notifications are designed to be unobtrusive and don’t require the user to close them. They automatically disappear within seconds.

...

Displaying long or complex information |Toast notifications are for brief messages that can be read and understood in the limited time that they’re shown on-screen, not for displaying long or complex information |If a software application has undergone a major update with a long list of changes, trying to communicate all of them through a toast notification would be very obtrusive |Linking to the changes via the toast notification might be more appropriate, but it depends on the exact scenario |

## How does the improper use of toast notifications affect the user experience?

Are you still wondering why it’s important to use toast notifications appropriately in your designs?

Well, this is important because toast notifications are designed to be unobtrusive, making it less likely for users to notice them adequately. Additionally, they lack a sense of urgency and can be unintentionally swiped away, causing users to miss critical information.

...

This scenario reflects the reality of how our customers typically engage with our products — skimming, scanning, or not paying full attention to every screen detail. This is why it’s crucial to empathize with your users to help you make informed decisions when implementing notifications.

## Best practices for designing toast notifications

To harness the benefits of toast notifications, try adhering to these three best practices:

### Place toast notifications out of the way

They shouldn’t be intrusive. Instead, they should be placed in the corner of the screen. Users somewhat expect them to be in the bottom-right corner, but if that option happens to obstruct something important on the screen, the top-right corner is okay too. Toast notifications are always going to obstruct something, so don’t worry about it too much.

### Get the auto-dismissal timings down

There’s no rule of thumb for the timing.

...

When toast notifications pop up, you’ll want to transition them subtly to ensure that users notice them. A simple slide-in from beyond the viewport should do fine — anything more than that is likely to annoy users.

However, you should suggest that developers use the [prefers-reduced-motion media query](https://blog.logrocket.com/new-in-chrome-74-prefers-reduced-motion-media-query-50cd89d3e769/) to disable the transition for those who can get sick from motion effects.

### Auto-dismissals aren’t accessible — here’s how to handle them

You have several options. You only need to provide one of them:

* Enable users to turn off the time limit before encountering it (e.g., in the settings)
* Enable users to adjust the time limit before encountering it (the extension must be at least ten times the default setting)
* Give users at least 20 seconds to extend the time limit by at least ten times the default setting with a simple action such as a keypress
You’re exempt from these rules if no alternative to the time limit is possible (e.g., if it’s part of a real-time event such as an auction), or if the time limit is more than 20 hours.

## FAQs about toast notifications

Below you’ll find the answers to some of the most frequently asked questions about toast notifications:

### Why are some notifications called toasts?

When a notification pops up but then disappears (typically after a few seconds), this is called a toast notification. As you might’ve guessed already, this is because when toast is ready, it pops up for a second and then disappears back inside the toaster. Quite a fun name, really.

### What is the difference between a toast and a banner?

Toasts are fixed-positioned (typically to the bottom-right corner of the screen), whereas banners typically appear unattached at the top of the main document. Toasts are for real-time alerts and messages, whereas banners are for ongoing ones.

...

* Should be neutral-looking, communicating a simple, non-critical message
* Can have interactive elements, but these too must be non-critical
* Must be accessible, although this falls under the jurisdiction of developers

By following these best practices and tips, you’ll be well on your way to creating great toast notifications.
